claims.text: Using advanced exchange-correlation functionals in DFT will improve predictive accuracy for heat transport in HfNbTaTiZr by at least 20% relative to previous approaches.
The proposed approach will predict lattice and electronic heat-transport contributions separately.
The claimed improvement applies below 200 K.
The claimed improvement applies from 300 to 1200 K.
The target material state is a bulk HfNbTaTiZr crystal that may contain defects and impurities, including approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
Atomic-scale complexity and defect structure mediate the effect of the proposed computational intervention on transport predictions.
Ab initio molecular dynamics or DFT with advanced exchange-correlation functionals provides the operative mechanism for improved prediction.
The proposed method will improve the separation and understanding of lattice and electronic heat-transport contributions.
Measured total thermal conductivity from 300 to 1200 K is 10–17 W/(K m).
The approach is applicable to bulk crystals containing potential defects and impurities.
Failure of the predictions to match measured lattice and electronic contributions within a 20% margin would falsify the hypothesis.
